sections.history: Tiruppanangadu lies about 16 km from Kanchipuram, near Cheyyar, in Tiruvannamalai district, in the old Thondai country. It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, sung in the Tevaram by Sundarar. The name means 'the forest of palms,' and the sthala vriksham is the palm tree. The structural temple carries Pallava and later work, in the Dravidian form of the Thondai Nadu shrines.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian temple of the Thondai country, the shrine enshrines Panankatteeswarar — Talapurisvarar, the lord of the palm-forest — and a second form, Kirubapurisvarar, with the goddesses Kirubanayaki and Amirtavalli, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The sthala vriksham is the palm. Worship begins at the lingam consecrated by sage Agastya, followed by the lingam of his disciple Pulasthyar.
sections.legends: The name Tiruppanangadu, 'the holy forest of palms,' is tied to a legend of sage Agastya and the palm fruit; by tradition he consecrated a lingam here, and his disciple Pulasthyar another, so that worship begins at Agastya's and passes to Pulasthyar's. Shiva is worshipped as Panankatteeswarar — Talapurisvarar — with the goddess Kirubanayaki. (This is a distinct shrine from Puravar Panankattur in Villupuram, another Paadal Petra Sthalam.)
sections.festivals: The temple holds its Brahmotsavam in Masi (February–March), the Annabishegam in Aippasi (October–November) and the Arudra Darshan in Margazhi (December–January), besides Maha Shivaratri and Pradosha worship. Pilgrims of the Thondai country include Tiruppanangadu among their stops.
sections.experience: At Tiruppanangadu the pilgrim comes to the lord of the palm-forest. Before Panankatteeswarar and Kirubanayaki, beginning at the lingam of Agastya, the visitor finds the unhurried grace of a Tevaram temple of the Thondai country, among the palms that give the place its name.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Tiruppanangadu lies about 16 km from Kanchipuram, near Cheyyar, in Tiruvannamalai district. Kanchipuram and Cheyyar are the nearest towns, with buses and taxis to the village; Kanchipuram is the nearest rail head.
